input.quote: (ii) an exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers, or (iii) a non‑exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable license, with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers ((i) through (iii) in order of preference), to PB of any Trial Invention that such Third Party contractor conceives, discovers, develops or otherwise makes in connection with activities conducted relating to this Agreement.
input.rationale: There is no conventional vendor-to-customer licence grant here: PB is the sole and exclusive owner of all Trial Inventions (11.1.1.3(a)) and acquires sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package (11.1.1.4), which is stronger than any licence. The only rights that reach PB as a licence are the flow-down licences SFJ must procure from its consultants and Third Party contractors under 11.1.1.3(b)-(c), and those are expressly "worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable ... with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers". Measured against the fallback checklist: PB's Affiliates are covered without even a written-notice mechanic, because PB may sublicense through multiple tiers and may freely assign; and the licence is transferable to a successor, both by its own "freely-assignable" terms and by Section 15.6, which lets either Party assign this Agreement and all rights to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, sale of stock or sale of assets without consent. Nothing is revocable at SFJ's discretion, and no clause excludes affiliates or contractors. This sits at (and in respect of affiliate/sublicence coverage above) the fallback position, so we do not redline it. Two preferred-only refinements are noted but not flagged: the fully-paid licences are not expressly labelled "perpetual" or "irrevocable", and SFJ's obligation to procure them is a commercially reasonable efforts obligation (11.1.1.3(c)/p0662). Neither is a material failure of the fallback, and PB's outright ownership of Trial Inventions makes the residual licence path a secondary safety net.
